header.name: Image, Screen, Interface
header.description:
This is an advanced class and requires you to read complex texts on a regular basis.
Our everyday lives involve dense interactions on various screens, transacting images over a range of interfaces. Today we find it in the technologically concretized form of the smartphone. But images have a dense material history. We begin our inquiry into images taking the dream as first site of investigation. We then move from the dream screen to look at painting. Photography is our next site of investigation as we examine practices of 'looking' at photographs. Next we study the cinema screen and our fascination with moving images. We develop a theory of 'the gaze' - a practice that looks as much outwards at the world, as it does inwards, inhabiting an imaginary or fantasy space - an internal screen. Having established a notion of imaginary inhabitation of internal screens, we move to a study of interfaces starting with machine gambling, and the relationship of 'addiction' to a machinic screen. We then study contemporary technologies such as algorithmic recommendation systems and big data analytics taking the edge of the interface as our point of entry. Finally, we examine ruptures to our inhabitation of the imagined space at the edge of screens and interfaces.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Develop an anthropological, philosophical and psychoanalytic understanding of images

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Understand screens as not merely technological, but as embedded in a social imaginary

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Examine the interface as a dense site of sociality
